text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) has applied for a judicial review of high court ruling which approved a government takeover of former president Kamuzu Banda's Press Trust, which ran the country's biggest conglomerate, Press Corp Ltd.

- Malawi's second-largest hotel, Blantyre Hotels Ltd (BHL) is listing 2.9 million ordinary shares on the Malawi Stock Exchange (MSE). BHL is the second company to list on the exchange. The first was National Insurance Company, which made its debut in the primary market in November last year.
- A South African woman was shot dead early on Saturday when police opened fire during a confrontation outside a nightclub.
- Junior Malawian police officers say their allowances have not been paid, while those of senior officers were paid immediately funds were available.

- The two opposition parties represented in parliament, Malawi Congress Party and Alliance for Democracy (Aford) have agreed to field one candidate in future byelections to ensure they do not split the opposition vote and give the ruling party a chance to win.
